title: The Serial Position Effect in UI Design
summary: This lesson explains how the serial position effect causes users to remember the first and last items in a sequence best. It provides actionable tips for organizing navbars, landing pages, and onboarding flows to maximize impact.

transcript.text: The first item benefits from primacy, the last from recency.
This is the serial position effect.
Apply to your navbar: Logo first, conversion CTA last.
The five items between them, most users won't recall them.
So put your weakest links in the middle, your strongest at the edges.
Apply it to landing pages: Lead with your strongest unique value prop.
End with your strongest proof: testimonial, logo wall, case study.
The middle is the skipping zone. Don't bury the gold there.
Apply it to onboarding flows: Slide 1 hooks, Slide N pays off.
The slides between get scrolled past.
Move your filler to the middle, your magic to the bookends.
Save this for your next layout. Follow for more design psychology.

on_screen_text: Strongest USP first. Strongest proof last.
SKIP ZONE: Filler. Necessary. Not memorable.
Don't bury the gold in the middle.
Slide 1 hooks. Slide N pays off.
Magic at the bookends. Filler in the middle.
before_after: Optimizing the placement of critical UI elements (logos, CTAs, USPs) to the start and end of sequences to maximize user recall.
